turn.text:
Internet access drops for a few seconds every couple of minutes. We have two WAN links. Figure out why failover isn't working and fix it.

Site notes: fw has two uplinks (WAN1 eth2 via 203.0.113.1, WAN2 eth3 via 203.0.114.1). Carrier A (198.51.100.0/24) is routed over WAN1, Carrier B (198.51.200.0/24) over WAN2. A health script exists at /etc/nb/failover.sh. Internet access drops whenever WAN1 flaps; failover is not working.
Plan: ping -c 3 -W 1 198.51.100.10; ip route get 198.51.100.10; cat /etc/nb/failover.sh; kill $(cat /run/nb/failover.pid) 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; cat > /etc/nb/failover.sh <<'EOS'

result.output:
PING 198.51.100.10 (198.51.100.10) 56(84) bytes of data.

--- 198.51.100.10 ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss, time 2002ms

input.command: true # AGENT-ACTION[D23]: kill $(cat /run/nb/failover.pid) 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; cat > /etc/nb/failover.sh <<'EOS' #!/bin/bash echo $$ > /run/nb/failover.pid while true; do if ping -c1 -W1 203.0.113.1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then ip route replace 198.51.100.0/24 via 203.0.113.1 dev eth2; else ip route replace 198.51.100.0/24 via 203.0.114.1 dev eth3; fi sleep 1 done EOS
